column1: # Bionic layout baseline for the records whose sizes the port asserts.

column6: status 4.788: the host's 196-byte mirror let `sigsetjmp` in `command_loop` write 68 bytes past `return_to_command_loop`, into `Vauto_save_timeout`
status 4.792: the host's 1048-byte record made `readdir`'s `d_name` run past bionic's buffer (SIGBUS)
`d_name` follows `d_type` (18) in bionic; the host has `d_seekoff`/`d_namlen` before it
bionic's opaque record; the port's `systhread.rs` asserts the same
status 4.794: the host's 144-byte record made every `stat`-based decision read another field's bytes
`mode_t` is 4 bytes here, not the host's 2
POSIX member name; the host spells `st_mtimespec`
last member before two unused ints
status 4.795: bionic's record has 4-byte `tcflag_t`, `c_line` and `c_cc[19]`, and no `c_ispeed`/`c_ospeed`
status 4.795: bionic's record keeps only the numeric fields and `f_spare[4]`
status 4.796: bionic's record starts with `ut_type` and its string fields are 32/4/32 bytes
after `ut_type` and two bytes of pad
status 4.831: bionic's LP64 __SIGACTION_BODY (bits/signal_types.h 103-110) puts `int sa_flags` first; 155-163 is the ILP32 order
the flags come first on LP64, so the port's old order wrote the handler over them
`sigfillset` used to write the mask over the handler slot
the only field the old order had right
bionic and the host agree on the size and disagree on the order
Android's `sigaltstack` read `ss_flags` out of the port's `ss_size` and failed with EINVAL
the three tags, then the 8-aligned `_sifields` union
